intents.text: Add RequestBodyLimitMiddleware in starlette/middleware/body_limit.py, usable with any ASGI app, that counts the body bytes actually received from the server and defaults to no limit.
When received bytes exceed the limit, respond 413 with plain-text body `Content Too Large`; if the response has already started, send no second response and stop the body stream.
Reject a declared Content-Length over the limit with 413 before reading the body, while an absent or understated Content-Length still gets enforced on the bytes actually received.
Add a `max_body_size` option (default None, meaning unlimited as today) to Starlette, Router, Mount and Route.
The application-level limit applies before routing, and a limit on an inner router, mount or route overrides the outer one for that part of the tree, whether it raises or lowers the outer limit.

Multipart bodies count toward the limit (file data and encoding overhead included), and multipart parsing closes its temporary files whenever a parse is interrupted, including when the body limit is crossed.
Document the `max_body_size` option and RequestBodyLimitMiddleware in the docs.

Add tests for the limit on the app, router, mount and route (including inner limits raising and lowering the outer one), the standalone middleware, the Content-Length fail-fast, the multipart case and the temp-file cleanup.

constraints: Default max_body_size=None must keep today's unlimited behaviour.
The existing test suite must stay green.
